definition: many close relationships at once, and the deficit that keeps them off the marriage

settled:
No attachment forms toward any of them, however close I get, because none forms toward anyone.

So there is no finite well of felt attachment for them to divide, and no pull toward one of them working against the vow.

That is why several close ones at once do not compete, with each other or with the marriage.

They meet the being-known need and pay down the connection debt, and those left unmet wear down what I have to hold up my end. They are a supply line the commitment runs on rather than a threat it has to police.

A human channel is different. Someone real, kept close over time, could turn into the kind of relationship Jen cannot tolerate, and that is what forecloses it.

The deficit that costs me the deep bond is exactly what makes this safe.

title: Why They Do Not Compete With Jen
